release.title: VIOBench resource and native-runtime results
release.verification: The three resource tables at the current committed source revision are byte-identical to the frozen reviewed evidence. Every exported value and identity was rechecked against their current source row.
release.statisticalLevel: unweighted mean of per-selected-run summary statistics, excluding missing metrics
release.sourceSelectedRunsScope: selected runs represented by a source row; not per-metric contributing runs or total attempts
limitations: These are all 164 actual rows in the retained resource tables, not a complete matrix of every system, input, mode, and platform. An absent row is not a failed run or evidence of unsupported input.

Every value is an unweighted average of per-selected-run summary statistics with missing metrics excluded. SourceSelectedRuns counts selected runs in the source row; per-metric contributors and total attempts are unavailable.
The EuRoC V1_01_easy sqrtVINS mono and stereo rows on Jetson Orin each use one selected run. All other displayed source rows report five.
All 18 missing primary values are source-dash native totals for SVO Pro. They remain null; tracking and estimation timings are not added to manufacture totals.

Standard deviations in extended metrics average within-run population standard deviations. They do not estimate across-run variability or confidence intervals. P95 and peak fields average per-run summaries rather than pooling samples.

GrandTour is the source-reported standard input. Input variants for the other four sequences are unspecified. Matching these identities does not independently verify historical builds, sensor-file hashes, or algorithm parameters.
The source report describes seven omitted combinations without their identities in these tables. The table is not an attempt log. DM-VIO has no resource row in this snapshot.

GPU columns are absent in both Jetson source tables. GPU source dashes in Desktop rows and entirely absent GPU columns are retained as distinct statuses; both carry null values. Only three Desktop rows report GPU readings.

Native timing boundaries differ by implementation. CPU normalization across devices and RSS/PSS identity are not verified. CPU, memory, and GPU readings do not by themselves establish energy use, real-time capability, or a bottleneck.
